title: Answer: no account of which systems are conscious, and the theory under test names the system

statements.text: The theorem takes no position on who or what is conscious and favors no particular state theory. It concerns accounts that assign consciousness to a bounded system such as a brain, a computer, a network or a mechanism, and the account itself names that system. For digital computers it sets a burden: until a physical property shared by every implementation of a computation is named, computation gives no state-sufficient basis for consciousness.
statements.scope: the no-go theorem, version 1 of the preprint
